summary: Stop a step's execution clock while its seat waits for a build slot or the merge queue, within one 12-hour wait budget per attempt

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes. The step timing fold gains a wait state that the checkpoint planner replays unchanged in shape; a node that runs older code ignores the new claim fields and charges a wait to the execution clock, so a step can time out sooner there, never later.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites. A wait is a work.progress claim with the optional fields clock and wait_until_unix_ms; the step view gains optional execution fields that are omitted when empty.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, retention, authority or admission rule change and no rules-version change. The claim schema registry digest changes because work.* claims accept the two optional fields; the existing registry upgrade rules apply.

compatibility.detail: Adds the work actions wait and resume (st work wait --for DURATION --reason TEXT, st work resume), the optional work.* claim fields clock and wait_until_unix_ms, and optional step view fields. Existing actions, claims and views are unchanged. A wait is accepted only from the holder of a live lease, needs a reason, and draws on 12 hours per step attempt; a request past the budget is refused with wait-budget-exhausted. Nothing calls the new actions until a seat or the host build queue adopts them.

downtime.detail: No startup work or expected interruption; the change adds no store migration and no new background work beyond one reconciler wake at a wait's end.

manual.detail: No operator actions or configuration changes are required. The host cargo build-slot queue should call st work wait and st work resume around its queue wait to benefit; that is host configuration outside this repository.

recovery.detail: No persistent state changes or new swap-back restrictions. An older node reading the new claims ignores the optional fields and charges waits to the execution clock again.
